title: AppMaker ADR v1
description: Formal schema for ADR documents under decisions/. Authored by WU-005 / ADR-003 based on actual structure used in ADR-001, ADR-002, ADR-003. Includes forbidden_patterns enforcement field per WU-004 lesson #7 (review).
description_note: ADRs are markdown documents, not JSON. This schema describes the META-LEVEL CONTRACT (which sections must be present, what counts as forbidden content, what bounds apply). A future implementation WU may build a markdown-to-structure parser that extracts these fields from an ADR file for validation. v1 enforcement is via shell-based grep / awk / sed checks at WU verification time.

required_sections.description: ADR top-level (## ) sections that MUST appear in declared order. Per ADR-001 / ADR-002 / ADR-003 conventions: 12 sections.

forbidden_patterns.description: String patterns that MUST NOT appear in ADR markdown body (governance discipline). Per WU-004 lesson #7 (review): parser/grep checks catch placeholders before VERIFIED. Mentions inside instructional contexts may need paraphrasing to avoid the literal token.

decisions_min_count.description: Minimum number of numbered decisions (D1, D2, ...) required in the Decision section.

killed_alternatives_min_count.description: Minimum number of killed alternatives (KA-1, KA-2, ...) required. Per constitution R1.

risks_min_count.description: Minimum number of risk rows required in Risks and Mitigations table.

length_bounds.description: Markdown line count bounds for the ADR file.

metadata_required.description: Metadata section must include: date, authors, type (investigation | implementation), supersedes, superseded_by.

lessons_applied_optional.description: When ADR is created by an investigation work_unit, lessons traceability table strongly recommended (typically inside §Decision-D[N]).

open_questions_recommended.description: Open Questions section enumerates what the ADR deliberately defers. Recommended for any non-trivial ADR.

rollback_plan_required.description: Soft + hard rollback paths must be documented.
